title: Grateful Dead Live at Bellarmine College on 1968-12-07
source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD D

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of an early Kentucky show with a smoking Dark Star > St. Stephen > Eleven and the only known live Rosemary, presented on decent but hiss‑prone audio.
ai_review.review: This recording documents a rare 1968 Louisville performance that deadheads rave about for its soaring Dark Star into St. Stephen and Eleven, plus the elusive Rosemary and a heartfelt Morning Dew. The Miller soundboard source is surprisingly clear for the era after Charlie’s hiss‑reduction work, though some tape noise and occasional roughness remain. Overall the show shines despite a few incomplete songs and one drummer’s illness that knocked out an Alligator request.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the music (rare Rosemary, strong Dark Star sequence) and deem the audio good for a 1968 soundboard despite hiss; weighted average of show (70%) and recording (30%) yields a high‑mid rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hiss present but reduced by Charlie's cleaning; overall clear for the era, some tape noise and occasional roughness on quieter numbers like Rosemary.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows well with a powerful second‑set jam, rare acoustic numbers, and a few incomplete songs (e.g., missing Lovelight) that don’t detract from the overall excitement.

band_member_comments.Drums: One of the drummers fell ill, leading to a missed Alligator request and a brief disruption during equipment repairs.
